body: We introduce SEA-HELM Audio, a Southeast Asian (SEA) multilingual evaluation framework that extends the text-based SEA-HELM benchmark to assess performance degradation in cascaded automatic speech recognition and large language model (ASR-LLM) pipelines. Using synthesized speech, we compare speech-input and text-input performance across five languages (Chinese, English, Malay, Indonesian, and Tamil) on multiple-choice reasoning and instruction-following tasks. We evaluate open-weight and commercial ASR-LLM systems using identical verifiers and quantify the speech gap as the difference between text and speech accuracy. Results show substantial degradation, with accuracy drops of 9.00 to 18.50 percentage points for multiple-choice reasoning and 20.00 to 42.86 points for instruction following. Tamil exhibits the largest degradation, exceeding 40 percentage points. Our findings highlight the limitations of text-only benchmarks in predicting voice-agent reliability and demonstrate the value of SEA-HELM Audio for evaluating multilingual voice-agent systems.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了SEA-HELM Audio，这是一个专门针对东南亚多语言环境的评估框架，旨在量化自动语音识别（ASR）与大语言模型（LLM）级联系统中的性能衰减。研究通过对比五种语言的文本输入与语音输入表现，发现语音输入在推理和指令遵循任务中存在显著的准确率下降，尤其在泰米尔语中表现最为严重。该基准测试为评估语音代理系统的鲁棒性提供了关键指标，并强调了仅依赖文本基准测试在预测语音交互性能时的局限性。
